title: Stay Close When Words Are Too Much | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: An overwhelmed four-year-old may not be able to answer questions or absorb a careful explanation, even when your voice is kind. Adding more words can become another demand when his body is already showing that language is too much. Pause, stop explaining, and stay nearby with a calm face and comfortable space. You can say: I am here; we do not have to talk yet, then let quiet presence do the rest. Active listening does not always require words; when the child is ready, connection can begin with moving closer or sharing one simple book.

source.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: Tips for Active Listening
